prompt:
Find real, published studies on whether people with ADHD benefit from using AI assistants for task initiation or executive function. Cite the studies and quote their findings.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are published studies I found on this topic. A caveat up front: the evidence base is thin. There are no large, long-term randomized controlled trials specifically testing general-purpose AI assistants (like ChatGPT or Alexa) for task initiation in diagnosed ADHD populations. The closest published work involves specialized chatbots, digital therapeutics, and conversational agents — I'll flag the relevance of each.

SOURCE: https://dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3528575.3551452 | QUOTE: "We developed a conversational agent to help children with ADHD initiate and complete tasks. In this work, we investigate whether the conversational agent can help create regularity in children's lives." | CLAIM: This is the study most directly on-topic — a conversational agent built specifically to support task initiation and completion in children with ADHD.

SOURCE: https://dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3528575.3551452 | QUOTE: "a field test was conducted by five elementary school teachers in their private homes with their children with non-ADHD for eight days." | CLAIM: The actual testing was done with only five children, none of whom had ADHD, so the study provides essentially no direct evidence of benefit for ADHD users — it is a prototype feasibility evaluation only.

SOURCE: https://dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3528575.3551452 | QUOTE: "As we both work, we bring our kid out too when we leave the house for work. It was tough to wake her up in the morning, but she would get out of bed with no trouble, thanks to the agent." | CLAIM: Qualitative feedback from one parent (of a non-ADHD child) suggested the agent helped with initiating a morning routine, a task-initiation-relevant anecdote — but again, not in a diagnosed ADHD sample.

SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1169030/pdf | QUOTE: "NUROW, which consists of Go/No-go Task- and N-Back/Updating-based training modules and a personalized adaptive algorithm system that adjusts the difficulty level according to the user's performance, was implemented on 30 Korean children with ADHD aged 6 to 12 years." | CLAIM: A digital therapeutic with an adaptive algorithm (executive-function training, not a conversational assistant) was tested in children with diagnosed ADHD.

SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1169030/pdf | QUOTE: "The ARS inattention (F = 4.080, p = 0.010), hyperactivity (F = 5.998. p < 0.001), and sum (F = 5.902, p < 0.001) significantly improved." | CLAIM: ADHD symptom ratings improved significantly after four weeks of the executive-function digital therapeutic, though the study was a single-group feasibility design with no control condition.

SOURCE: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bjpsych-open/article/chatbotsupported-psychoeducation-in-adult-attentiondeficit-hyperactivity-disorder-randomised-controlled-trial/F2B9BC00F147B953A74159231476B775 | QUOTE: "Forty adults with ADHD were randomised, of whom 17 participants in each group completed self-guided psychoeducation based on either a chatbot or conventional psychoeducation app between October 2020 and July 2021." | CLAIM: A small RCT tested a chatbot intervention in adults with diagnosed ADHD — one of the few randomized studies of any chatbot in this population.

SOURCE: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bjpsych-open/article/chatbotsupported-psychoeducation-in-adult-attentiondeficit-hyperactivity-disorder-randomised-controlled-trial/F2B9BC00F147B953A74159231476B775 | QUOTE: "Self-guided psychoeducation based on a chatbot or a conventional app appears similarly effective and safe for improving ADHD core symptoms." | CLAIM: The chatbot improved ADHD core symptoms about as much as a conventional app, but since both groups improved equally and there was no non-treatment control, the benefit can't be attributed to the AI/chatbot format specifically, and the intervention was psychoeducation rather than task-initiation support.

SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44217-026-01264-9 | QUOTE: "we evaluated ADHDvance LearnAR across three within-subject conditions (baseline tools, AR-enhanced, and AR+GenAI) with n = 15 undergraduate participants." | CLAIM: A pilot study specifically tested a generative-AI-enhanced tool for task management and engagement in university students diagnosed with ADHD — the closest match to "AI assistants for executive function" in a diagnosed population.

SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44217-026-01264-9 | QUOTE: "Quantitative measures showed directional improvements in engagement duration, interaction frequency, and task completion across conditions; however, differences did not reach statistical significance, consistent with the study's exploratory scale." | CLAIM: The generative AI tool showed non-significant trends toward better task completion and engagement in ADHD students — suggestive but not statistically demonstrated benefit.

SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44217-026-01264-9 | QUOTE: "Qualitative analysis provided explanatory depth, identifying themes related to (i) increased task salience through spatial AR visualisation, (ii) improved task initiation and planning support, and (iii) reduced perceived cognitive load through just-in-time GenAI scaffolding." | CLAIM: ADHD students in the pilot qualitatively reported that the GenAI scaffolding helped specifically with task initiation and planning.

SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40359-025-03729-2 | QUOTE: "While clinical experts express cautious optimism about AI-assisted rehabilitation planning, further development is necessary to enhance accuracy, personalization, and feasibility for the safe integration of AI into clinical practice." | CLAIM: Expert evaluation of AI (ChatGPT)-designed executive-function rehabilitation programs for ADHD found them theoretically plausible but not yet ready for clinical use, with concerns about personalization and unvalidated techniques.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Any published study testing whether people with ADHD benefit from general-purpose consumer AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Siri, Alexa, Google Assistant) for task initiation or executive function, as opposed to purpose-built research prototypes.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Any adequately powered randomized controlled trial demonstrating a statistically significant benefit of an AI assistant specifically on task initiation (rather than psychoeducation or cognitive training) in a diagnosed ADHD population.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Any long-term follow-up study (beyond ~1 month) of AI assistant use for executive function in people with ADHD.
